business_rules.statement: Lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly, and there are no exceptions by work type, risk class, or tag.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Lot release service in the Delivery Operations Hub

business_rules.statement: The Severity 1 minimum action bundle of automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation is platform-fixed and tenants may never remove it.
The creator of a Job cannot approve that same Job; separation of duties is satisfied by any second holder of the approving role.
The Studio approval chain runs Author, then Reviewer, then Release Authority, with the Reviewer a different person from the Author and no role performing two stages on one submission.
Evidence is immutable; corrections are append-only annotations carrying who, when and what changed, with the original never altered.
business_rules.applies_to: All roles including Quality Manager and Worker

business_rules.statement: Undecided Lane B proposals age with a 30-day stale flag and never expire silently; the decision is always human.
An approved package-borne Lane B value auto-publishes as a patch version; a server-only value applies immediately.
A quality engineer is a persona, not a role; authoring is carried by an authoring grant layered on the Supervisor or Quality Manager role.
Removal of the last approver-capable role while Jobs exist is refused.
A release decided while target devices are offline renders as propagating, per device, never as globally released.
No mutating operation succeeds for the Read-only Auditor on any surface, through any interface; any mutating request is refused and recorded as a security-relevant event.
An unavailable audit source renders an explicit unavailability message, never an empty result; an empty audit view is a dangerous rendering.
There is no on-device worker override: no gate in the application can be overridden by the worker it blocks.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Frontline Worker Application gate screens and device API

business_rules.statement: A blocked run parks and the worker continues with their other assigned runs; the parked run resumes when the clearance arrives.
Attribution is always by individual identity, never by device, and there is no cap on concurrent workers per run.
Every worker has their own platform identity and login; the credential is the person's, never the device's.
Captured media stays in the application's encrypted store and never touches the device gallery under any condition, including wipe, storage pressure and app upgrade.
Sync state renders per item with distinct states and never as a single completion word.
A sync is forced before sign-off as a designated high-risk action.
Every tenant role cannot override a specification gate or the evaluation gate from any surface.
No tenant role can pause or stop a run from the Client Command Center.
No tenant role can edit any record or configuration from the Client Command Center.
No tenant role can create Jobs or runs from the Client Command Center.
No tenant role can make any configuration looser than the platform floor.
No tenant role can alter or delete evidence or audit history.
No tenant role can reach another tenant or the Super Admin platform console.
The platform stores no object of kind persona; a job title may be recorded only as free-text reference metadata and is excluded from every authorization decision.
Every audit entry names the acting identity. No audit entry contains an acting as role field.
Every effective permission resolves to at least one of: a role type, a scope, a grant, a qualification, or a temporary grant. No other source of authority exists.
A name qualifies as a role only if it appears in the five-row tenant table or the four-row console table; nothing else is a role.
The platform exposes no create-role, edit-role, or clone-role control on any surface at V1; the roles endpoint returns exactly nine role types.
Escalation routing accepts roles only; recipients are selected as roles, never individuals; personas are reachable only through the additional recipient list, which confers no authority.
A scope narrows a role and never widens it; the three scope dimensions are held simultaneously and are orthogonal.
A grant is additive and time-bounded and may never create authority a role does not already contain; the authoring grant adds authoring but cannot add approval or release.
Every non-human identity has a named human sponsor — a specific accountable human being holding a specific role, not a team name.

No non-human identity may cross a tenant boundary except where the source explicitly makes the component cross-tenant, and then only on anonymised aggregates or within a named, audited, session-scoped access class.
business_rules.enforcement_point: ENFORCED platform invariant, locked with no off position

business_rules.statement: No non-human identity is an approver. Approval on this platform is human, everywhere.
Every action a non-human identity takes commits with its audit event in the same transaction. An action that cannot be audited does not happen.
No non-human identity can be provisioned without all eighteen fields populated and an approved change-approval record; critical-class capability escalates to the root.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Identity record validation and change-approval cycle

business_rules.statement: No user interface on any surface displays a provisioned credential value at any time, including at the moment of creation.
A failed rotation moves the identity to Suspended and raises a platform alert; it never extends the existing credential.
The non-human identity register offers Suspend and Revoke controls and offers no Create control.
A device identity contributes zero permissions to any authorization decision; removing the worker's login from a request causes refusal regardless of device identity.
A wipe command is displayed with its true state and is never displayed as applied before an acknowledgement is received.
Every Command Center operational action executes through the Delivery Operations Hub service that owns the record, under the acting human's identity, with identical rules.
The inbound enterprise-resource-planning and application-programming-interface endpoints return 501 at V1 and create no records.
Command delivery is idempotent: a redelivered command applies once and is acknowledged once.
The platform exposes exactly two notification channels, in-app and email, at every tier and on every surface; in-app notifications cannot be muted by any role including the Tenant Admin.
An email failure never changes a hold, a gate, a qualification block, a suspension, or a command's state.
The finish is the one automatic transition in the platform — a data-integrity rule, not a status change.
No scheduler is an approver. A scheduled execution may publish, distribute, compute, tier, or anonymise. It may never approve.
Every scheduled execution occurrence carries exactly one tenant context and is refused if it attempts to act outside it.
A missed occurrence is recorded as a misfire with its due time and detection time and is never silently dropped.
A stale worker whose lease expired is refused by the fencing token and cannot double-apply an occurrence.
A manually triggered scheduled run records the triggering human identity, not the scheduler identity, as the initiator.
No automation identity re-bases an in-flight run; version pinning holds through every publication.
Detection is deterministic, interpretation is agentic; no artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path; agents activate only after a deterministic trigger.
No model participates in the deviation-triggering path; disabling every model leaves severity classification and the Severity 1 hold fully operational.
The embedding index contains only approved corpus content, is scoped to one tenant, and never contributes to another tenant's retrieval.
An emergency pause parks in-flight agent runs at their next stage boundary, leaves raised gates human-decidable, and never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
No write operation of any kind is reachable inside a normal support session; a support-tool credential cannot be used outside an open session and dies at session end.
Reading record-level operational content is impossible outside the three named access classes, on every console route. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
Offboarding cannot complete until every active and upcoming run assignment is reassigned; open step executions close as abandoned with the recorded reason "Worker departed".
No account transition deletes, hides or alters any capture, evidence item, or audit entry.
Re-employment reactivates the prior record with history intact and presents a re-validation prompt; no prior qualification is silently re-trusted.
Anonymisation never runs for a tenant in Regulated-Industry mode; anonymisation is the lifecycle's one irreversible act.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Anonymisation scheduler reading the tenant-configuration registry

business_rules.statement: A revocation that would remove the last Tenant Admin, or the last approver-capable holder while a Job exists, is refused with the specific rule and object named.
A grant in RevocationPending is never displayed as fully revoked on any surface.
A queued action is validated against current authorization at application, never at queueing.
Actions already completed under a grant remain valid and attributed after the grant is revoked.
Platform console role changes are performed only by the root account; there is no role-escalation path except the root acting.
Authorization is evaluated at every action submission, not only at session open or screen render.
A second-identity step-up never ends or alters the worker's session and is recorded against exactly one authorisation.
The Frontline identity strip displays a person's name and never a role name.
A device's local capture queue survives logout, session expiry, and worker switching; the queue belongs to the device, not to the session.
The trust window governs authorization only; on-device severity classification, specification gates, and the Severity 1 hold operate regardless of its state.
In the restricted state, work in progress completes and no new run starts under cached authority.
Reconnected, Revalidated and Reconciled are three distinct, separately displayed states; no surface collapses them into "synced".
The warning schedule fires at exactly 14, 7, 1 and 0 days; a tenant may add earlier stages and cannot remove or delay any stage.
At expiry under strict posture, the worker completes the entire current run and the next assignment requiring that certification is blocked; there is no grace period beyond it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Step-level enforcement on the mobile device

business_rules.statement: Self-attestation of a qualification is impossible on every surface; qualifications are supervisor-entered with a full audit trail.
A recertification whose new expiry does not postdate the old is refused.
A clearance lapses automatically at the tenant-set duration and returns the certification to expired, never to active.
A second clearance in the same Area on the same shift routes to the Quality Manager regardless of which worker it concerns.
Notify-only posture produces notifications and audit flags in place of blocks and is the floor; no configuration produces a silent posture.
The qualification gate is the only configurable gate on the platform; the specification gates and the evaluation gate are hard and non-configurable.
No delegation object exists at V1 on any surface, and no user interface offers a delegate-my-authority control; cover is an ordinary role grant and revocation.
The absence of an approver never causes an automatic approval on any surface, at any tier, for any object.
The compliance-emergency session cannot open on fewer than two authorisations, one of which is the root; the declared scope is fixed at open and cannot be widened.
The compliance-emergency path is the only path with write capability into tenant data from the console, and the only entry into a compliance-suspended tenant.
An automatic post-session report is generated for the tenant on every close, including a close by time-box expiry.
No session of any class makes an offline device appear remotely controlled.
Suspending any non-human identity leaves on-device specification gates, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold fully operational.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Deterministic backbone with no off switch

business_rules.statement: Rotation uses an overlap period so that no request fails during changeover; suspension of a non-human identity destroys no data and drops no queued work.
The compliance-suspension worker-facing message is fixed verbatim: "Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved."
Late captures arriving inside the tenant's finish window fold in flagged late_arrival; after finish, the audited-recompute rule applies.

decisions.question: What does the Supervisor+ plus notation mean for the ten Command Center operational actions and the substitute sign-off?
options: union-with-explicit-deny model (recommended, not adopted)
literal role-type reading
decisions.adopted_working_position: Both readings preserved; every authority statement names explicit role types; a union-with-explicit-deny model recommended but not adopted
decisions.impact: Governs six of the ten Command Center actions and substitute sign-off

decisions.question: Are Plant Manager and Quality Director personas, a composed user group, or a fixed role?
options: Reading A — the closure reading: five tenant roles, both names are personas
Reading B — the user-group reading: role plus scope plus landing view, plus an escalation recipient class
Reading C — the fixed-role-table reading: a sixth fixed role in the Studio access table
decisions.adopted_working_position: Build on Reading A. Never render "Quality Director" as a role in any user interface.
decisions.impact: Reading C would move the role count from nine to ten and re-issue every permission matrix

decisions.question: How does the Quality Manager's Lane B authority sit against the three-stage approval chain?
decisions.impact: Referenced in the Quality Manager card; not resolved

decisions.question: Is the nobody-on-shift escalation default to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift correct?
decisions.adopted_working_position: Escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback delivery
decisions.impact: Referenced in the Supervisor and Quality Manager cards; not resolved

decisions.question: The Studio module count is derived, not stated.
decisions.adopted_working_position: Rendered as derived wherever a count appears
decisions.impact: Affects every Studio module count statement

decisions.question: Atom enablement authority versus tenant current-value authority.
decisions.adopted_working_position: Both readings preserved in both cards
decisions.impact: Affects the Admin and Platform Engineer cards

decisions.question: The capture-type set differs between the platform contract and the Studio.
decisions.adopted_working_position: The §5.5.3 set of seven capture types: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or Quick Response code scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, and dropdown selection
decisions.status: adopted working position, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Governs the Worker card's capture functionality enumeration

decisions.question: Does a reconnecting device upload pending captures before or after pulling pending commands?
options: upload first
download first
option C — three phases
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted 2026-08-14 in three phases — stop-class commands pulled and applied first, then every pending capture uploads with nothing discarded, then the enabling-class commands apply
decisions.status: adopted working position, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Affects the worker's reconnection experience and the offline lifecycle ordering

decisions.question: What is the device storage-full behaviour?
decisions.status: deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification; no behaviour invented
decisions.impact: Referenced in the Worker fallback data treatment

decisions.question: How long may a wipe command remain pending, and what happens if the device never returns?
decisions.impact: Affects the root's device-targeting powers and lost-device containment

decisions.question: Does the work package carry all three difficulty levels?
decisions.adopted_working_position: The package definition carries all levels until resolved
decisions.impact: Affects the Worker card and package composition

decisions.question: The surface name divergence.
decisions.adopted_working_position: The Statement of Work name is used throughout these chapters
decisions.impact: Naming across surfaces

decisions.question: May a JBS access grant carry write capability into tenant data, given that §8.15.2 calls the compliance-emergency path the only write-capable class?
options: Read-only always (recommendation, not adopted)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client platform operations lead with the JBS engagement lead

decisions.question: Do the tenant-visible banner and the tenant End-session control apply to the compliance-emergency path and the JBS access grant, or only to the normal support session?
options: Banner on all three; End-session on the support session and the JBS grant only (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client legal and compliance owner

decisions.question: May the Root Super Admin act as checker on a Platform Engineer change, or is Admin the only checker?
options: Root may check only where no Admin account is enabled, with a recorded continuity reason (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client platform operations lead

decisions.question: Does any class of platform access into tenant data require the Tenant Admin's affirmative consent before it opens?
options: Consent for JBS grants only; visibility for the client's own support (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client commercial and legal owner

decisions.question: Is the placement of a legal hold disclosed to the affected tenant?
options: Disclose unless a non-disclosure flag is set at placement (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client legal owner

decisions.question: Who holds root custody, who are the two break-glass custodians, what is the tolerable root outage, and what out-of-band identity verification applies?
options: Two custodians, neither holding the credential in ordinary operation, with a rehearsal cadence (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client platform operations lead with the security owner

decisions.question: May a support session be extended beyond its time box, by whom, and how often?
options: No extension; always a new session (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client support operations lead

decisions.question: May a support engineer export anything from inside a session?
options: No export; findings written in prose (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client security owner with the tenant data-protection owner

decisions.question: Does the Studio authoring grant or the Agent Author delegation carry an expiry or a periodic re-affirmation?
options: Perpetual until revoked, with a mandatory annual review report (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: tenant quality lead with the client product owner

decisions.question: Which role may perform a substitute sign-off on a worker device when no Supervisor is available, given that the five roles are additive and unordered?
options: Quality Manager only (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client product owner with the tenant quality lead

decisions.question: May the Read-only Auditor export, and if so exactly what, for what purpose, under what controls, and with what audit?
options: Option A, no export
Option B, defined export with controls
Option C, unrestricted export (rejected in this blueprint)
decisions.adopted_working_position: Export is rendered as `Client Decision Required` in every matrix cell for this role. No fragment assumes it exists.
decisions.impact: Recommendation is Option B with mandatory categorised reason at export time

decisions.question: What Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective apply to the access decision path and the other fallback contracts in these chapters?
options: Minutes-scale for the access decision path specifically (recommendation)
decisions.impact: Decision owner: client platform operations lead

decisions.question: Which console role holds platform on-call for the 2-hour connectivity-loss escalation?
options: (a) escalate to the Admin role at platform scope
(b) escalate to a named recipient list configured in Observability settings
(c) build a platform on-call rota object
decisions.impact: An escalation with no resolvable recipient fails silently, which the honesty rules forbid

decisions.question: What does "impersonation control" in §4.12.3 mean — a guardrail preventing impersonation, or a control panel for an impersonation feature?
options: (a) confirm the guardrail reading and strike the phrase
(b) specify an impersonation mechanism requiring a fourth named access class, dual authorisation, tenant-visible banner and tenant-side mirroring
decisions.impact: An undocumented impersonation capability would breach tenant isolation, audit completeness and the three-access-class closure

decisions.question: What per-role account ceilings apply, given the commercial model meters Worker-Shifts and not seats?
options: (a) no ceilings
(b) a soft advisory threshold surfaced in the tenant administration area
(c) hard per-role caps carried in the tier record
decisions.impact: Recommendation option (b) for Tenant Admin and Quality Manager only; decision owner client product owner with the commercial lead

decisions.question: Delegation is deferred, yet the Agent Author capability is described as delegated — assignment semantics or a genuine delegation object?
options: (a) confirm assignment semantics and correct §5.18's wording
(b) build a scoped delegation object for capabilities only, not for roles
decisions.impact: A delegation object carries an expiry and a delegator-of-record; an assignment does not

decisions.question: What device-bound credential mechanism is issued at enrollment (the standardised device profile is owed by the client)?
decisions.impact: Blocks the device identity credential type

decisions.question: What are the deprecation, disablement, rollback and in-flight fate rules for agents, including composed agents?
decisions.impact: Agent expiry and disablement are not stated

decisions.question: Does the Prevention Agent operate entirely under pre-authorised policy, or does every action agent route through a human gate before any effect?
options: §3.7 and §6.6.1 reading: entirely pre-authorised policy, runtime gate only for proposals beyond it
§8.3.2 and §8.3.3 reading: action agents every one routes through a human gate; Prevention Agent labelled action, gated
decisions.adopted_working_position: Governance bound to `authoring-time policy`, declared on the agent record
decisions.status: adopted working position, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Determines whether the Prevention Agent needs a runtime human gate

decisions.question: Who launches the containment checklist — the device at classification or the Deviation and Containment Agent?
decisions.adopted_working_position: The device launches it locally at classification, never the agent
decisions.impact: Bounds the Deviation and Containment Agent's permissions

decisions.question: Session timeout, concurrency, and survival across permission changes on the three tenant-facing web surfaces.
options: (a) a single platform default with no tenant configuration
(b) a tenant setting bounded by the floor register
(c) per-surface values, with the Command Center shorter
decisions.impact: Recommendation option (b): 8 hours absolute lifetime, 30 minutes inactivity, concurrency limit 3, oldest terminated on the fourth

decisions.question: Is 24-month anonymisation confirmed under the no-purge model?
decisions.impact: Remains open and is not resolved in the account lifecycle section

decisions.question: The scheduled-work family open questions, DEC-SCHED-001 through DEC-SCHED-010 as enumerated in the commission.
decisions.impact: Carry the open questions for the scheduling identity family

contradictions.description: §3.5 states there is no Quality Director and fixes five roles; §6.1.3 lists "Plant Manager / Quality Director" as a Command Center user group; §5.18 lists Plant Manager as a row in a table headed Fixed role.
conflicting_values: five fixed tenant roles, both names are personas (Reading A)
a composed user group with landing view and escalation position (Reading B)

contradictions.description: The phrase "everything a Supervisor sees" for the Quality Manager on the Command Center is one of the readings feeding the plus notation dispute.
conflicting_values: Quality Manager holds everything a Supervisor sees plus record-affecting authority
Supervisor+ actions may require a separately held Supervisor role

contradictions.description: The Quality Manager's Lane B authority (single human decision, auto-publish as a patch) sits against the Studio's three-stage approval chain.
conflicting_values: Lane B approved value auto-publishes as a patch version with no second approval
Author then Reviewer then Release Authority chain with no role performing two stages

contradictions.description: The capture-type set differs between the platform contract and the Studio.

the platform contract set

contradictions.description: Upload-versus-download ordering at reconnection is not stated by the source.
conflicting_values: upload pending captures first
pull pending commands first
three phases: stop-class commands, then uploads, then enabling-class commands (adopted 2026-08-14)

contradictions.description: §4.8.1 states the Read-only Auditor is read-only across the tenant including the full audit log; §3.5 and §6.12.2 say report-format authoring and export is a Tenant Admin and Quality Manager capability, leaving auditor export unstated.
conflicting_values: read-only across the tenant including the full audit log
export is a Tenant Admin and Quality Manager capability

contradictions.description: §4.12.3 lists "cross-tenant visibility and impersonation control" while Part VIII defines no impersonation feature, states support sessions are read-only without exception, closes access classes at three, and forbids an acting-as-role record.
conflicting_values: impersonation control means the control that prevents impersonation (guardrail)
impersonation control means a control panel for an impersonation feature, implying a fourth access class

contradictions.description: §4.8.4 defers delegation beyond V1 and §4.13 lists role delegation as out of V1 scope, yet §5.18 and §5.15.4 describe the Agent Author capability as held or delegated and as an Agent Author delegation.
conflicting_values: Delegation is deferred beyond V1; cover is manual role add and remove
The Quality Manager holds or delegates the Agent Author capability; a delegated administrator may hold compose authority

contradictions.description: §3.7 and §6.6.1 say the Prevention Agent operates entirely under pre-authorised policy with the runtime gate only for proposals beyond it; §8.3.2 says action agents every one routes through a human gate before any effect and §8.3.3 labels the Prevention Agent action, gated.
conflicting_values: entirely pre-authorised policy, runtime gate only beyond policy

contradictions.description: The Scheduler Controller and the Scheduled Execution Worker are named in the blueprint commission but the source names no such components; they are User-Mandated Product Extension, not contracted.

contradictions.description: The source says the finish is the one automatic transition in the platform, while tiering, anonymisation and Lane B auto-publish are also automatic acts.
conflicting_values: the finish is the one automatic transition — a data-integrity rule, not a status change
tiering and anonymisation are lifecycle acts on storage and identity, not business-state transitions

contradictions.description: The 24-month anonymisation horizon sits against the platform's no-purge lifecycle model.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No Quality Manager on shift when a Severity 1 hold lands; release command cannot reach an offline device; gate item times out; Lane B proposal ages past 30 days; last Quality Manager removed while Jobs exist
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no Quality Manager can be reached, the hold stays in force and the affected lot, unit or run remains quarantined; the Tenant Admin is notified as an administrative escalation but still cannot release the hold
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The hold remains in force, the anomaly remains Open, and production on the affected lot remains stopped
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Quality Manager decides; the release travels as a command; devices acknowledge; the anomaly closes with a note

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A mutating route reachable by the Read-only Auditor through an API the UI does not expose; the audit log is unavailable; a scope assignment is wider than the audit requires
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Any mutating request from this role is refused and recorded as a security-relevant event
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the audit log is unavailable, reads continue for other objects and the audit view renders an explicit unavailability message naming the log rather than an empty result
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The role reads what is available and is told plainly what is not; no inference of completeness is offered
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The log returns; the view refreshes; no data was lost because nothing is purged

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Connectivity lost for an extended period; cached credential ages past the offline trust window; a qualification gate blocks with no clearance; device storage fills; clock skew beyond threshold; device lost or stolen
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Offline execution continues from the version-pinned package with local detection, classification and containment
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: When the trust window expires the worker cannot start new work on that device and must authenticate; existing committed captures remain committed and queued
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device holds committed captures in its encrypted store, enforces gates locally, and holds any Severity 1 hold in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection; captures move through their states to officially recorded; pending commands download, validate and apply in order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A surface renders for a role that should be prohibited; a scope filter fails open; the Studio serves a draft to a read-only role
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The response is withheld and the request refused
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The surface is disabled for the affected role pending investigation, with an explicit banner rather than a blank screen
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Affected roles lose the surface; execution on the Frontline Worker Application continues
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The defect is corrected; assertions pass three consecutive times; the surface re-enables

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A decision is answered informally and implemented without updating the permission set, the cards, the tests and the published views
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The implementation is treated as unapproved and is not shipped until the decision is recorded properly
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where already shipped, it is recorded as an unapproved behaviour, the decision is formalised retrospectively, and any tenant affected is informed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The interim behaviour stated in each decision card remains in force — in every case the more restrictive option
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The six-step closure workflow, ending with tenants reconciled and differences reported

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The permission-resolution service cannot resolve an account's effective permission set at login — the role store is unreachable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The platform refuses the login and states the reason plainly; no cached or assumed permission set is granted on a web surface
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated resolution failure across a site raises the connectivity-loss protocol timers: 30 minutes, 60 minutes, 2 hours
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Web surfaces are unavailable for authentication; the Frontline Worker Application continues offline inside the trust window; the deterministic on-device layer is untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Resolution service restored; sessions re-established by fresh login, never by silently reviving a stale session

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An administrator attempts to create a role named after a job title
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The platform has no create-role path at V1; the Roles pane offers no create control
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The administrator assigns a mismatched role to approximate the title; the platform cannot detect intent, so this is a governance risk
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No role is created; the tenant continues with the nine role types; operations unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Custom roles are a stated post-V1 roadmap item and arrive with their own approval discipline

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant's escalation configuration names a target the platform cannot resolve because the intended recipient is a persona rather than a role
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The role picker offers only roles; the additional-recipient list absorbs the persona case without creating authority
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The configured role has no holder on shift when the escalation fires; escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The escalation is recorded as delivered-by-fallback and remains open and unacknowledged; the Severity 1 hold is unaffected and remains in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On the next shift, the Quality Manager acknowledges and resolves; both are distinct timestamped states

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The counts drift because an implementer adds an authority object without registering it
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The tenant-configuration registry rejects out-of-bound values outright and the roles endpoint returns a fixed nine
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: An object is added through a backend migration without registry representation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform continues on registered objects; an unregistered object is treated as absent by every permission check
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The object is registered through the change-approval cycle or removed by the same migration path

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The onboarding mapping leaves a tenant with an author who is also the only approver
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The worksheet's live validation strip blocks commit while the check is red
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant commits a valid mapping and later removes the second approver; the narrow case of one approver-capable holder who authors everything is not covered by a mandatory-role rule
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The submission cannot advance; the Workflow stays unpublished; the floor continues executing the previously published version because in-flight runs are version-pinned
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Tenant Admin assigns Quality Manager to a second person, or configures a per-workflow Release Authority override

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An identity record is submitted with a mandatory field empty — commonly field 11 prohibited actions or field 13 offline behaviour
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Submission is refused at validation with the missing field named; the record stays in Drafted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Platform Engineer fills the field with a placeholder; detection is the Admin approval step and the rule that an empty prohibitions field is itself a review finding
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The identity is not provisioned; no credential exists
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The record is completed and resubmitted

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device is lost while offline holding unsynced captures
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: De-authorisation is issued and a wipe command created; the sync-then-wipe rule requires a final sync attempt before erasure
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device never contacts the platform again; the wipe cannot be applied — DEC-WIPE-001 is unresolved
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The wipe command remains queued, visibly pending and never shown as applied; the device is de-authorised platform-side; the captures are recorded as an evidence gap
failures_fallbacks.recovery: If the device returns, the final sync runs, captures fold in flagged late arrival where inside the finish window, and the wipe applies

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The command-channel service identity is unavailable, so no command can be delivered to any device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Commands accumulate in their durable queue in the created and queued states
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The outage outlasts the shift; every surface must continue to display each command's true state
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Decisions are recorded but not delivered; the on-device deterministic layer places holds locally; a lot stays held longer than intended, which is the safe side
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The identity is restored; queued commands drain in order; superseded commands are recorded as superseded rather than deleted

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The email vendor is unavailable platform-wide during a Severity 1 escalation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: In-app delivery, a separate channel that cannot be muted, carries the escalation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The recipient is not looking at an in-app surface; the acknowledgement timer lapses; unacknowledged Critical notifications re-notify after 4 hours, or 1 hour in Regulated-Industry mode
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The lot remains frozen; the Severity 1 minimum action bundle is platform-fixed and does not depend on anyone reading anything
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The vendor returns; queued email drains; delivery states advance

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Scheduler Controller stops evaluating definitions during a platform incident; no run auto-close occurrences are created
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Due occurrences are recorded as misfires when the Controller returns; nothing executes early and nothing executes twice
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Many misfires accumulate; running them at once would distort scheduled reports; the misfire policy governs — run late in due order with a rate bound
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run records stay complete longer than the tenant's window, which still accepts late captures; Command Center run states remain honest
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Controller resumes; misfires are worked in due order under the policy; the fencing token prevents a record finishing twice

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The primary model router role degrades platform-wide
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Failover to the fallback router role per the configured failover thresholds
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The fallback role also degrades; the lightweight role serves what it can; agents requiring the primary role become unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Agent unavailability, never silence; the deterministic backbone is untouched — gates, specification checks, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold continue with no off switch
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Router roles restored; in-flight agent runs that checkpointed at a stage boundary resume; raised gates remained human-decidable throughout

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A support-tool identity attempts a write during a session, whether by defect or by misuse
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The write is refused at the session boundary; no write capability exists inside a normal support session
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated refusals indicate a defect or attempted misuse; both are visible through the tenant banner, the mirrored audit entries and the console-side action count
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant's data is unchanged; the ticket remains open; the correct escalation is the compliance-emergency path
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The defect is fixed through the change-approval cycle, or the misuse is handled as a personnel matter with the audit record as evidence

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An account is suspended for cause while the person is mid-run on an offline device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The suspension applies server-side immediately and rides the command channel; the device applies it at next sync, in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device does not reconnect; the offline credential-trust window bounds the exposure at the tenant-set value, default ~24 hours, ceiling 72 hours
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: At the end of the trust window the cached credential is no longer trusted; the device refuses further work; work already captured is preserved locally
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The device reconnects; the suspension applies; preserved captures upload

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A role is revoked while the holder has actions queued on an offline device that depend on that role
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Queued actions are validated at application, not at queueing; an action whose authorising permission no longer exists is rejected at application and recorded as rejected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The rejection leaves a worker parked at a qualification gate expecting a clearance that will never arrive
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run parks; the worker continues other assigned runs; nothing is auto-approved because a permission lapsed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A current Supervisor or Quality Manager grants the clearance afresh; it rides the command channel and takes effect at next sync

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A session's permission set is reduced mid-action — the person begins a Quality-Manager-only action and the role is revoked before they submit it
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Authorization is checked at submission, not only at screen render; the submission is refused with a stated reason
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The person retries and is refused again; the action does not occur
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action is not performed; for a lot release the lot remains held and the Command Center shows the hold as still in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A current holder of the authority performs the action

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A worker's access is revoked at 08:00 while their device has been offline since 06:20
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The revocation applies server-side immediately and is queued as a command; the device is unreachable
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device remains offline; the revoked worker continues working on cached authorization
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The trust window bounds the exposure at ~24 hours, never more than 72; at the boundary the device restricts, at the restricted bound it blocks; captures are preserved in full
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The device reconnects; the revocation applies in command order; the session terminates

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A qualification expires mid-shift and no supervisor is available to grant a clearance
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The supervisor is notified immediately through the standard escalation path and decides remotely
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The notification is unacknowledged within the configurable window, default 2 minutes, and escalates to the Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run parks; the worker continues their other assigned runs; no work is done under an expired certification and no clearance is granted automatically
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Supervisor or Quality Manager grants the clearance, or a qualified substitute is assigned, or the run is cancelled with a categorised reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An approver is absent unexpectedly and no cover has been granted
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Escalation resolves to holders of the target role on shift
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No holder of the target role is on shift; escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A controlled hold: a Job stays in pending approval, a gate item ages, a lot stays held; nothing is approved because time passed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A Tenant Admin grants the covering role, following the manual procedure

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An urgent data repair is needed and the root account is unreachable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The compliance-emergency path cannot open on one authorisation; no fallback to single authorisation exists and none may be created
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The situation deteriorates while the root is unreachable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The repair does not happen; tenant data remains unchanged and fully evidenced; the operational instruments (lot hold, suspension, emergency pause) remain available and the deterministic on-device layer continues
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The root, whose custody rests with the client, is reached; the session opens properly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A non-human credential is suspected compromised
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Immediate suspension by an Admin, which does not wait for the approval cycle
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The dependent platform function is now unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The function degrades to its declared FB-* contract with honest surface communication; the on-device deterministic layer is untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A replacement identity is provisioned through the approval cycle and activated; queued commands drain in order; fencing tokens refuse stale duplicates

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device unavailable

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: unstated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: unstated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-enrollment as a new device identity; a wiped device never resumes its previous identity

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Backend service unavailable

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: unstated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: unstated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Credential rotated, identity reactivated, queued work drained in order

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Email unavailable

failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: unstated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No notification is ever the sole enforcement of anything
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Vendor restored; queued email drains; each notification's email leg resumes its state machine
